preview.subtitle: The classic seal-in circuit. Press START and STOP and watch power flow through the rung.
preview.explanation: The motor contact, in parallel with START, keeps the circuit closed after you release the button: that is the seal-in (latch). STOP uses a normally closed contact, which opens when pressed and breaks the circuit.

scan.label: Interactive scan cycle diagram

read.name: Read inputs
read.description: The PLC copies the state of every physical input into the input image. From now until the next cycle, the program works with that copy.

execute.name: Execute program
execute.description: The program runs from top to bottom using the input image. Results are written to the output image, not to the terminals yet.

write.name: Write outputs
write.description: The output image is copied to the physical outputs: only now does the lamp turn on or off.

housekeeping.name: Diagnostics and communication
housekeeping.description: The PLC serves communications (HMI, programming device), checks its own health and resets the cycle-time watchdog. Then it starts over.

scan.hint: Flip the switch at any moment: the PLC will only notice it in the next “Read inputs” phase.

sensor.label: Wiring diagram of a three-wire sensor to a PLC input
sensor.object: Object in front of the sensor
sensor.legend: BN = brown (+24 V) · BU = blue (0 V) · BK = black (signal)
sensor.pnpOn: The PNP sensor connects the black wire to +24 V. Current enters the PLC through I0.0 and returns to 0 V through the common.
sensor.npnOn: The NPN sensor connects the black wire to 0 V. Current enters the PLC through the common from +24 V, leaves through I0.0 and flows into the sensor.
sensor.off: With no object, the sensor's internal switch is open: no current flows through the input and the PLC reads 0.

analog.label: Analog level signal simulator
analog.currentFault: 0 mA is outside the 4–20 mA range: the PLC detects the fault.
analog.voltageFault: 0 V looks like an empty tank: the fault goes unnoticed.

terminals.title: Compact PLC with its terminals and ports
terminals.hint: Click (or use Tab and Enter) on a terminal, LED or port to see what it is and how it is wired.
terminals.empty: Select a part of the drawing.
terminals.generic: Generic drawing of a compact 24 VDC PLC with relay outputs. Terminal positions and names change with brand and model: always check the manual.

power.name: Power supply (L+ and M)
power.what: Terminals through which the PLC gets its power. On 24 VDC models, L+ is positive and M is negative (0 V). AC-powered models are marked L1 and N.
power.connect: From the panel's 24 VDC power supply, protected by a circuit breaker or fuse. Mind the polarity and use the wire size given in the manual.

pe.name: Earth (PE)
pe.what: Earth connection. It helps drain electrical interference and, on devices with metal parts, protects people.
pe.connect: With green/yellow wire, as short as possible, to the panel's earth bar.

inputCommon.name: Input common (1M)
inputCommon.what: Common point of the input group: it closes the circuit of every input in that group.
inputCommon.connect: To 0 V when using PNP sensors (sink input) or to +24 V when using NPN sensors (source input). Check in the manual whether the module accepts both.

inputs.name: Digital inputs (I0.0 to I0.7)
inputs.what: Each terminal receives the signal of a push button, selector, limit switch or sensor.
inputs.connect: One wire per signal from the field device. On a 3-wire sensor, brown goes to +24 V, blue to 0 V and black to the input terminal.

statusLeds.name: Status LEDs
statusLeds.what: They show the PLC mode: RUN (running the program), STOP (stopped) and ERROR (hardware or program fault).
statusLeds.connect: Not wired. They are the first thing to look at when checking a panel.

modeSwitch.name: RUN / STOP selector
modeSwitch.what: Some models have a physical selector to stop or start the program without the software.
modeSwitch.connect: Not wired. On many current devices the mode is changed from the software or a screen.

ioLeds.name: Input and output LEDs
ioLeds.what: One LED per point. They show the electrical state of the terminal, not what the program says: a lit input LED means voltage reaches that terminal.
ioLeds.connect: Not wired. They tell you whether a problem is in the wiring (the LED does not light) or in the program (the LED lights but the program does not react).

ethernet.name: Ethernet port (RJ45)
ethernet.what: The most used port today: programming and communication with HMI screens, SCADA systems and other PLCs, using protocols such as Modbus TCP, PROFINET or EtherNet/IP depending on the brand.
ethernet.connect: With network cable (category 5e or higher; shielded in noisy environments) to a switch in the panel.

rs485.name: RS-485 serial port
rs485.what: Serial bus communication, widely used with Modbus RTU for drives, meters and older equipment. Several devices share the same pair of wires, over distances of up to about 1200 m at low speed.
rs485.connect: With shielded twisted pair, joining A to A and B to B (some manufacturers swap the A and B marking). The bus has 120 Ω termination resistors at both ends.

usb.name: USB port
usb.what: Used to connect the computer and download or check the program.
usb.connect: With a short cable, only for programming and diagnostics. It is not used as a permanent connection in a plant.

sdCard.name: Memory card slot
sdCard.what: Depending on the model, the card backs up the program, updates the firmware or stores data logs.
sdCard.connect: Use only the card type given by the manufacturer. On some devices, removing it while the PLC is running stops it or raises an error.

expansion.name: Expansion connector
expansion.what: Side bus to add modules: more inputs and outputs, analog signals or communications.
expansion.connect: Modules are mounted side by side on the rail. Connect them with the PLC powered off, unless the manufacturer allows hot swapping.

outputCommon.name: Output commons (1L and 2L)
outputCommon.what: On relay outputs, they feed the contacts of each group. Each group can work at a different voltage, for example 24 VDC on one and 230 VAC on another.
outputCommon.connect: To the phase or positive to be switched, with a fuse matching the group's maximum current.

outputs.name: Digital outputs (Q0.0 to Q0.5)
outputs.what: Contacts the PLC opens or closes according to the program. They drive pilot lights and the coils of contactors, solenoids or interface relays.
outputs.connect: From the output terminal to the load, and from the load to neutral or 0 V. Large loads, such as a motor, are always driven through a contactor.

dinRail.name: DIN rail
dinRail.what: The PLC snaps onto a standard 35 mm metal rail inside the panel.
dinRail.connect: Leave space above and below for ventilation and cable ducts, as the manual specifies.

languages.label: IEC 61131-3 languages
languages.intro: The same program in all five languages: motor start and stop with seal-in. Switch tabs to compare them.

notes.LD: Contacts in series are AND; in parallel, OR. The MOTOR contact in parallel with START is the seal-in. STOP is an NC push button, so it is examined with an NO contact.
notes.FBD: The same operations as blocks: ≥1 is OR and & is AND. The MOTOR output feeds back into the OR block.
notes.ST: A single line with text operators. ST is ideal for calculations, complex conditions and loops.
notes.IL: Assembler-like instructions on an accumulator: load (LD), operate (OR, AND) and store (ST). The standard's 3rd edition (2013) deprecated it and the 4th (2025) removed it, but it still shows up on older equipment.
notes.SFC: Describes the process as steps and transitions. The motor runs while step S1 is active (N action). SFC shines in multi-stage processes.

diagnostics.MISSING_OPERAND: An address or variable must be assigned.
diagnostics.UNKNOWN_SYMBOL: “{operand}” is neither a valid address nor a variable in the table.
diagnostics.RUNG_WITHOUT_OUTPUT: The rung has no output coil.
diagnostics.EMPTY_BRANCH: A parallel branch is empty: it acts as a bridge that always conducts.
diagnostics.INVALID_ADDRESS: Address {address} does not exist in this PLC.
diagnostics.READ_ONLY_TARGET: {address} is a system bit: it can only be read.
diagnostics.INPUT_WRITE: Input {address} is written: the value will be overwritten in the next scan.
diagnostics.DUPLICATE_OUTPUT: Output {address} is written in {count} places: only the last one counts (duplicate coil).
diagnostics.UNDEFINED_TEMP: Internal error: temporary {name} is not defined.
diagnostics.TYPE_MISMATCH: Wrong data type: {expected} was expected but {actual} was given.
diagnostics.INVALID_INSTANCE: “{instance}” is not a valid instance: use T0–T31 for timers and C0–C31 for counters.
diagnostics.DUPLICATE_INSTANCE: {instance} is used in {count} places: they share the same timer or counter.
diagnostics.ST_UNCLOSED_COMMENT: A comment is opened and never closed: “*)” is missing.
diagnostics.ST_UNKNOWN_TYPE: “{type}” is not an available type. Use BOOL, INT, REAL, TIME, TON, TOF, TP, CTU, CTD, CTUD, R_TRIG or F_TRIG.
diagnostics.ST_UNKNOWN_NAME: “{name}” is not declared: add it to the variable table, declare it in VAR or use an address such as I0.0.
diagnostics.ST_NOT_CALLABLE: “{name}” is not a function block: declare a TON, CTU, R_TRIG… in VAR.
diagnostics.ST_UNDECLARED_FB: Declare the type of “{name}” before calling it, for example: VAR {name} : {example}; END_VAR
diagnostics.ST_MISSING_PARAM: Parameter {param} is missing in the call to {name} ({type}).
diagnostics.ST_DUPLICATE_CALL: {name} is called more than once: each edge detector is called once per cycle.
diagnostics.ST_NAME_CONFLICT: “{name}” already exists in the variable table or is an address: use another name.
diagnostics.ST_NO_FREE_MEMORY: There is no free memory left for “{name}”.
diagnostics.ST_BAD_INIT: “{name}” does not accept an initial value.
diagnostics.ST_UNKNOWN_FUNCTION: Function {name} is not available. You can use conversions such as TO_REAL, TO_INT or TO_TIME.
diagnostics.ST_UNSUPPORTED: “{feature}” is not available in this simulator yet.
diagnostics.ST_CASE_LABEL: CASE labels must be integers, such as 1, 2..5 or -1.
diagnostics.ST_FOR_VARIABLE: A FOR variable must be an integer (INT): “{name}” is not.
diagnostics.ST_FOR_STEP: The BY step of a FOR must be a constant integer other than 0.
diagnostics.ST_EXIT_OUTSIDE_LOOP: EXIT can only be used inside a FOR, WHILE or REPEAT.

scan.title: Scan cycle
scan.intro: Watch the scan cycle step by step: the PLC reads every input, runs the rungs in order, writes the outputs and starts over.

explain.idle: Press “Visualize” to walk through the cycle slowly. Meanwhile, you can operate inputs on the panel.
explain.read: Input terminals are copied to the input image. From now on the program sees these values, even if you flip a switch.
explain.execute: Rung {n} was executed: its results are now in the output image and the markers.
explain.write: The output image was copied to the terminals: only now do the output LEDs change.
explain.housekeeping: The PLC serves communications and checks itself. Cycle {n} is over; the next one begins.
explain.executeSt: The ST program ran from start to end: its results are now in the output image and the markers.

help.title: ST quick reference
help.intro: Use names from the variable table or addresses such as I0.0, Q0.0 and MW10. Ctrl+Space shows suggestions.
items: Assignment: MOTOR := START AND NOT STOP;
Comparison: =, <>, <, >, <=, >=   Logic: AND, OR, XOR, NOT
Comments: (* … *) or // to the end of the line
Your own variables: VAR count : INT := 0; END_VAR
Timer: VAR t : TON; END_VAR  t(IN := START, PT := T#5s);  Q0.1 := t.Q;
Counter: VAR c : CTU; END_VAR  c(CU := SENSOR, R := RESET, PV := 10);
Edge: VAR e : R_TRIG; END_VAR  e(CLK := BUTTON);  IF e.Q THEN … END_IF;

brands.indexDescription: Comparison of Siemens, Allen-Bradley, Schneider Electric, Mitsubishi Electric, Omron, ABB, Delta and WEG: product ranges, programming software, free or paid licences and address notation.
brands.intro: What you learn here applies to any brand, but each manufacturer has its own ranges, software and way of naming addresses. This guide helps you find your way.
brands.noPrices: We do not publish prices: they change by country, distributor and version. We use qualitative ranges.
brands.compareIntro: Filter the brands by what matters to you. The software column shows each brand's most accessible option.
codesys: CODESYS is an IEC 61131-3 programming environment made by an independent company. Many manufacturers use it as the base of their own software, for example ABB (Automation Builder), Schneider Electric (EcoStruxure Machine Expert) or WEG (PLC500).
Its development system is a free download. What you pay for is each device's runtime licence; without it, the trial software PLC runs in demo mode for a limited time.
That is why learning CODESYS pays off: what you know works across several brands.
brands.expensiveTitle: Why is some software so expensive?
expensive: Small ranges usually come with free or cheap software: the manufacturer earns by selling many devices and wants getting started to be easy.
In large ranges the software is part of a system that runs whole plants: CPU redundancy, functional safety, motion control, HMI and SCADA integration, teamwork and version control.
The licence includes technical support, updates and compatibility with equipment installed for decades. In a plant, one hour of downtime costs far more than the licence.
To learn you do not need the most expensive tool: the concepts (contacts, timers, scan cycle) are the same, and free or trial versions are enough to practise.

about.title: About this site
body: {site} is an independent educational project for learning PLC automation. It is not affiliated with any PLC or industrial software manufacturer.

trademarks.title: Trademarks
body: Brands and product names mentioned belong to their respective owners and are used only to identify products for educational purposes. We do not use official logos.
Product and software information is checked against official sources on the date shown on each page, but it may change: always check the manufacturer's site.

education.title: Educational scope
body: The content and the simulator are for learning. They do not replace professional training, equipment manuals or applicable standards.
Do not use this site to design or validate real safety systems. Work on electrical equipment must be done by qualified personnel.

privacy.title: Privacy
body: There are no accounts or forms: we do not ask for or store personal data on a server.

To work, the site stores in your browser's local storage your preferred language and theme, the simulator project, the address style and your challenge progress. That data never leaves your device and you can delete it from your browser settings.
We use privacy-friendly visit analytics (Vercel Web Analytics) that provides aggregated, anonymous data and uses no cookies.
We do not show ads today. If they are ever added to content pages, this policy will be updated first and your consent will be requested where required.

body: Some pages link to third-party sites (manufacturers, payment providers). We are not responsible for their content or their privacy policies.
